# Mahāpuṇṇama Sutta (MN 109 (PTS MN iii 15))

**ID:** MN 109 (PTS MN iii 15)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Mahāpuṇṇama Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** The Longer Discourse on the Full-Moon Night
**PTS:** MN iii 15
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāpuṇṇama Sutta* (MN 109) is set at Sāvatthi in the Eastern Park, in the Palace of Migāra's Mother, during a fifteenth-day Uposatha full-moon night as the Buddha sits in the open surrounded by the monastic Saṅgha [Shi Huifeng & Orsborn 2012; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. A monk presents the Buddha with a catechistic sequence of questions regarding the five aggregates affected by clinging (*pañcupādānakkhandhā*), their origins and cessation, the formation of personality view (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*), and the realization of non-self (*anatta*) [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. When the doctrine of not-self is expounded, another monk misconstrues it, wondering who will experience the karmic fruition of actions if there is no enduring self—an erroneous assumption the Buddha explicitly corrects [Anālayo 2014]. As the discourse concludes, sixty listening monks attain full liberation of mind from the taints (*āsavas*) [Bodhi 2003]. In commentarial taxonomy, Buddhaghosa's *Samantapāsādikā* lists the *Mahāpuṇṇama Sutta* among the *vedalla* class of texts—discourses elicited through repeated questioning that feature profound, subtle analysis [Nyanatusita 2013; Walser 2005].

- [Shi Huifeng & Orsborn 2012] Shi Huifeng (M. B. Orsborn), Chiasmus in Early Prajñāpāramitā (2012) — Documents the standard opening setting formula at MN iii 15 on the full-moon Uposatha night.

- [Anālayo 2014] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Perspectives on Satipaṭṭhāna (2014) — Discusses the monk's misunderstanding regarding karma, retribution, and non-self in the sutta and its SĀ 58 parallel.
